{{short description|American statistician}}
'''Rebecca A. Betensky''' is a professor of [[biostatistics]] and chair of the department of biostatistics at [[New York University]]'s School of Global Public Health.{{r|nyu}} Previously, she was a professor of biostatistics at the [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]], where she directed the biostatistics program for the Harvard Clinical and Translational Science Center. She was also a biostatistician for [[Massachusetts General Hospital]], where she directed the biostatistics core of the Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center.{{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
Betensky studied mathematics as an undergraduate in [[Harvard College]], graduating in 1987. She completed a doctorate in statistics at [[Stanford University]] in 1992.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, supervised by [[David Siegmund]], was ''A Study of Sequential Procedures for Comparing Three Treatments''.{{r|stan|mgp}}

After postdoctoral studies at Stanford, she joined the faculty of [[Northwestern University]] in 1993.{{r|cv}} She returned to Harvard as a faculty member in 1994, recruited as part of a large [[National Institutes of Health]]-funded contract for Harvard to perform statistics for the [[AIDS Clinical Trials Group]].{{r|cv|sin}} She became associated with Mass General in 2007.{{r|cv}}

In 2018, she joined the faculty of New York University's School of Global Public Health as professor and chair of the department of biostatistics.{{r|nyu-announce}}

==Awards and honors==
Betensky has been a [[fellow of the American Statistical Association]] since 2003, and an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] since 2007. She won the Mortimer Spiegelman Award of the [[American Public Health Association]] in 2005.{{r|cv}} In 2023 Betensky was awarded Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. <ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 AAAS Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/2023-fellows |access-date=2025-03-06 |website=www.aaas.org |language=en}}</ref>
